name: KP Energy Ltd
tagline: KP-group wind BoP / EPC contractor plus a small IPP - FY26 PAT ~Rs 181 Cr (ATH), ~9x earnings, ~Rs 3,000 Cr / ~2.2 GW order book - cheap and growing, but the market discounts it for heavy reliance on group company KPI Green as its main customer, and management over-promised on FY26
business_overview: KP Energy Ltd (BSE/NSE: KPEL), part of the KP group (Faruk Patel), develops utility-scale wind power infrastructure: wind-site siting, land and permits, EPCC, and balance-of-plant (BoP). It also owns and operates WTGs and a solar plant as an IPP (~48.5 MW: 37 MW wind + 11.5 MW solar), targeting ~100 MW by FY27.
fundamentals_table: 2026-05-08: Q4FY26 sales +58% YoY to Rs 632 Cr; net profit +72% YoY to Rs 79 Cr; OPM 18% -> 21%; QoQ sales +83%, PAT +93%
Guided ~Rs 2,500 Cr revenue / ~Rs 275-300 Cr PAT; delivered ~Rs 1,505 Cr / ~Rs 181 Cr - a large miss (still ~60% growth)
fundamentals_narrative: KP Energy screens cheap and fast-growing: FY26 revenue ~Rs 1,505 Cr, PAT ~Rs 181 Cr (record), ~9x earnings, OPM stepping up to ~21%, and a ~2.2 GW / ~Rs 3,000+ Cr order book (~2x revenue) against a real wind-capex tailwind. The ValuePickr thread (12355) explains the persistent discount: KP Energy is, in effect, a captive EPC arm - 'most of the order book is from KPI Green' (the group solar entity), so a large share of revenue and margin depends on a related party (Umang_Adatia, Jan 2026). Management also over-promised: after its first-ever concall (Nov 2024) it guided ~Rs 2,500 Cr / ~Rs 275-300 Cr PAT for FY26 and delivered ~Rs 1,505 Cr / ~Rs 181 Cr - a ~40% revenue miss, even though growth was still ~60%. Promoter holding fell from ~69% (2020) to ~45% (2023) when a co-promoter exited, then stabilised around 45% (Faruk Patel has since nudged his stake up) - a historical concern, not a live collapse. No formal red flag, but RPT dependence + guidance credibility are the reasons the multiple stays at ~9x.
technical_read: Not pulled - Tier-A escalation not warranted at this conviction.
sentiment_summary: Thread 12355 (kp-energy-lotus-in-muddy-water, cat 19, 96 posts). First-time deep read of the most recent ~35 posts. Sentiment has improved since the 2020-2022 wind-policy slump (reverse-bidding turmoil, Gujarat HC land petition - since resolved in the company's favour). Recent posts (2024-2026) are constructive on growth and order book but repeatedly circle back to two issues: dependence on KPI Green as the main customer, and management's tendency to guide high and deliver lower.
community_signal: No live trusted-roster call. basumallick posted a wind-sector overview in Feb 2023 (18 likes) but that is a sector primer, not a stock call. Community view: growth and cheapness acknowledged; the group-customer dependence is the accepted reason for the discount.
key_new_facts: Order book ~2.22 GW / ~Rs 3,000+ Cr, ~2x FY26 revenue - but a large share sourced from group company KPI Green (KP Energy acts as EPC contractor for KPIL).
FY26 delivered ~Rs 1,505 Cr revenue / ~Rs 181 Cr PAT vs the ~Rs 2,500 Cr / ~Rs 275-300 Cr management had guided - a significant miss (guidance credibility: mixed / over-promises).
IPP portfolio ~48.5 MW (37 MW wind + 11.5 MW solar), targeting ~100 MW by FY27 - a growing annuity layer.
Promoter holding stabilised ~45% after a co-promoter exit (down from ~69% in 2020); Gujarat HC land petition resolved in the company's favour.
OPM stepped up ~18% -> ~21% in Q4FY26; QoQ sales +83%, PAT +93% (lumpy, execution-timing driven).

value_chain.theme: Wind power - balance-of-plant / EPC + small IPP
value_chain.position: Wind-site development, EPCC and balance-of-plant contractor (does not supply the turbines - customers order WTGs directly); also a ~48.5 MW wind+solar IPP
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Wind-site pipeline (land, permits, evacuation) and execution bandwidth; turbine supply and financing sit with the customer
value_chain.note: India's wind build-out (RE targets, repowering, hybrid tenders) is a genuine multi-year tailwind. KP Energy's BoP/EPC niche is real, but its order book is materially tied to group company KPI Green, which caps the pricing power and the multiple the market will pay.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: FY25 ~Rs 940 Cr revenue / ~Rs 115 Cr PAT; FY26 ~Rs 1,505 Cr / ~Rs 181 Cr (+~60% / +~57%); Q4FY26 sales +58% YoY, PAT +72%, QoQ +83% / +93% - strong but lumpy on execution timing.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: ~9x trailing with ~60% growth and a 2x-revenue order book is cheap on growth; the market is holding the multiple down for RPT dependence and the FY26 guidance miss, not for lack of growth.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Reinvesting in the IPP (targeting ~100 MW) and EPC capacity; part of the KP group with inter-group order flow (KPI Green is a major customer)
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Adding an owned-IPP annuity layer alongside the EPC/BoP contracting base

bull_case: Cheap (~9x earnings / ~1x sales) with FY26 PAT at a record ~Rs 181 Cr and ~60% growth
~2.2 GW / ~Rs 3,000+ Cr order book (~2x FY26 revenue) against a real wind-capex tailwind
OPM stepping up (~18% -> ~21%); growing owned-IPP annuity layer (~48.5 MW -> ~100 MW target)
Gujarat HC land dispute resolved in the company's favour; promoter holding stabilised
bear_case: Order book materially dependent on group company KPI Green - KP Energy is largely a captive EPC arm, which caps pricing power and the multiple
Management over-promised on FY26 (guided ~Rs 2,500 Cr / ~Rs 275-300 Cr PAT, delivered ~Rs 1,505 Cr / ~Rs 181 Cr)
Wind BoP/EPC is a low-multiple, execution-timing-driven, working-capital-heavy activity
Promoter holding ~45% (down from ~69% in 2020 after a co-promoter exit); RPT trend a concern
verdict_headline: Cheap, fast-growing wind BoP/EPC contractor with a 2x-revenue order book - scored 10x-in-2-3-years at Low conviction, unconfirmed, with the KPI-Green customer dependence and FY26 guidance miss as explicit caps on the re-rate
verdict_reasoning: Sovrenn-news seed (tier 4.65). The Sovrenn trigger (Q4FY26 sales +58% YoY, PAT +72%, OPM 18% -> 21%) holds up and FY26 PAT is a record ~Rs 181 Cr. Per the trailing-vs-live rule: strong trajectory + a 2x-revenue order book + a cheap small-cap -> 10x-in-2-3-years at Low conviction with an 'unconfirmed' caveat.

The thread supplies the caps: the order book is largely sourced from group company KPI Green (KP Energy is effectively a captive EPC arm), and management guided ~Rs 2,500 Cr / ~Rs 275-300 Cr PAT for FY26 but delivered ~Rs 1,505 Cr / ~Rs 181 Cr. Both hold the multiple at ~9x for good reason and cap the re-rate a true 10x would need. rpt_trend 'concerning', guidance_credibility 'over-promises', management assessment 'concern'.

Promoter holding ~45% (down from ~69% in 2020 after a co-promoter exit) has been stable since - a historical concern, not a live collapse, so no HIGH CAUTION tier. No SEBI/auditor issue. Live-theme: wind is not a listed active theme (EV/BESS priority-2 is only adjacent). conviction Low-Medium; revisit_after_30d false. Re-check on FY27 delivery vs guidance and any reduction in KPI-Green revenue concentration.

four_box.note: Verdict: India's wind build-out is 'a genuine multi-year tailwind' (yes); but order book materially tied to group co KPI Green explicitly 'caps the pricing power and multiple' (moat=no); '~9x trailing... cheap on growth' (valuation=yes).
